 SSI payments are coming out early. Why that's happening for November
 Sarah Moore, USA TODAY NETWORK 2026년 10월 27일 화 오후 1:19 UTC 0 The final wave of Social Security payments for October will be distributed this week, and the November payment for Supplemental Security Income also is going out this week — earlier than usual.
 Michigan recipients of Social Security may expect their last payment for the month of October on Wednesday, Oct. 28.
 A few days later, recipients of Supplemental Security Income or SSI receive their payments on Friday, Oct. 30 ― earlier than usual because checks are typically sent out on the first of each month.
 Social Security is paid through the Social Security Administration to benefit retired workers, those with disabilities or for survivors. The Supplemental Security Income program is also a part of the SSA to provide benefits for those with limited or no income or resources, those aged 65 or older and those with a qualifying disability.

 Why are Supplemental Security Income payments going out this week?
 Beneficiaries of SSI will receive their checks earlier than usual in November. Checks will be delivered on Friday, Oct. 30, rather than the normally scheduled date ― which is the first of each month ― because Nov. 1 lands on a Sunday.
 When will I see my Social Security payments in November?
 Here are the payment dates for Social Security checks in November:
 Wednesday, Nov. 10, for Social Security beneficiaries with birth dates between Sept. 1-10.
 Wednesday, Nov. 18, for Social Security beneficiaries with birth dates between Sept. 11-20.
 Wednesday, Nov. 25, for Social Security beneficiaries with birth dates between Sept. 21-31.
 When does the cost-of-living adjustment go into effect? 
 Recipients of SSI and Social Security will receive a 3.6% increase to their benefits in 2027. 
 SSI payments will increase starting Dec. 31, 2026, while Social Security benefits will see the change in January 2027, according to the Social Security Administration .
